notes: All three with-skill runs scored 100%. The one baseline miss was eval-0 not passing --no-tokenizer; it worked only because the in-repo Shakespeare corpus loaded, so the HF-download gotcha the skill front-loads was left unguarded.

Because this repo's CLAUDE.md is unusually detailed and crates/mock-rs source is easy to find, the baselines self-recovered most gotchas (127.0.0.1, --ttft/--itl, reading app.rs for routes). The skill's measurable edge is therefore mostly SPEED and TOKEN COST, not correctness: with-skill averaged ~75s faster and ~3.5k fewer tokens per task by skipping source-spelunking.

Non-discriminating assertions (both configs always passed): the 127.0.0.1 checks, the --ttft/--itl checks, active-liveness checks, and route enumeration. In a leaner repo without the rich CLAUDE.md these would discriminate more; here they mostly confirm the skill doesn't regress correctness.

eval-1 baseline produced a RICHER aiperf command (added --tokenizer/--concurrency/--synthetic-input-tokens-mean) than the with-skill run — a hint the skill's aiperf-wiring section could show a fuller example.
Single run per (eval, config) — no within-config variance captured. Deltas are directional, not statistically robust.
